question: Under South Carolina's child care center regulations (S.C. Code Regs. 114-500 to 114-509), what is the staff-to-child ratio for children from birth to one year at a licensed child care center in South Carolina? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: STAFF:CHILD RATIOS Child's Age Staff:Child Ratio Birth to one year ... 1:5
notes: Ratios apply whenever children are on the premises and during activities away from the center. The nap-time ratio for this age is also 1:5.

question: Under South Carolina's child care center regulations (S.C. Code Regs. 114-500 to 114-509), what is the staff-to-child ratio for children three to four years old at a licensed child care center in South Carolina? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: STAFF:CHILD RATIOS ... Three to four years ... 1:12
notes: During nap time the ratio is 1:24 if at least one other staff person is readily available (114-504.C(1)). Mixed-age groups without infants or toddlers use the ratio for the age of the majority (114-504.B(2)).

question: Under South Carolina's child care center regulations (S.C. Code Regs. 114-500 to 114-509), what is the staff-to-child ratio for children four to five years old at a licensed child care center in South Carolina? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: STAFF:CHILD RATIOS ... Four to five years ... 1:17
notes: During nap time the ratio for children four and older is 1:34 if at least one other staff person is readily available (114-504.C(1)).

question: Under South Carolina's child care center regulations (S.C. Code Regs. 114-500 to 114-509), what is the staff-to-child ratio for children six to twelve years old at a licensed child care center in South Carolina? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: STAFF:CHILD RATIOS ... Six to twelve years ... 1:23
notes: Children five to six years: 1:20.

question: Under the general qualifications for caregivers/teachers at a licensed child care center in South Carolina, what is the minimum age?
quote: Caregivers/Teachers shall meet the following: (i) Be at least 18 years of age, and able to read and write;
notes: Exception: a 17-year-old may work as a teacher/caregiver with a GED or high school diploma if continuously supervised by a qualified teacher/caregiver who is in the room at all times (114-503.K(4)(c)).

question: Under South Carolina's child care center regulations (S.C. Code Regs. 114-500 to 114-509), a director of a licensed child care center in South Carolina who qualifies with a high school diploma or GED plus Early Childhood Development (ECD) 101 must also have how many years of experience in a licensed, approved or registered child care facility?
quote: (v) A High School Diploma or GED, and Early Childhood Development (ECD) 101 with 3 years' experience in a licensed, approved or registered child care facility. One year shall include supervision of child care staff.
notes: One of five alternative qualifications (114-503.K(3)(c)(i)–(v)). One of the three years must include supervising child care staff. The director must also be at least 21.

question: How many clock hours of training must staff who provide direct care to children at a licensed child care center in South Carolina complete each year (not counting emergency persons and volunteers)?
quote: All staff, with the exception of emergency person(s) and volunteer(s), providing direct care to the children shall participate in at least fifteen clock hours annually.
notes: CPR and first aid training do not count. Must include OSHA blood-borne pathogens training. Up to five excess hours may carry over (114-503.K(5)(d)). Directors need 20 clock hours (114-503.K(5)(b)).

question: What is the minimum indoor play space per child at a licensed child care center in South Carolina?
quote: The director shall provide at least thirty-five (35) square feet of indoor play space per child, measured by Department staff from wall to wall.
notes: Department staff measure and compute each room separately to set the number of children per room.

question: What is the minimum outdoor play space per child at a licensed child care center in South Carolina?
quote: The director shall provide at least seventy-five (75) square feet of outdoor play space per child. Where outdoor space is insufficient at the center, the director and/or staff may take the children outdoors in shifts
notes: The rule says 'per child' without saying whether that means licensed capacity or children outside at one time. If space is short, children may go out in shifts or use nearby parks.

question: What is required before staff at a licensed child care center in South Carolina give a child any prescription or over-the-counter medication?
answer: Written, signed and dated parental consent.
quote: Written, signed and dated parental consent is required prior to the administration of any prescription or over the counter medication or administration of special medical procedures
notes: Special medical procedures must also be ordered in writing by a physician or other legally authorized healthcare provider (114-505.D(1)(c)).

question: How often must a licensed child care center in South Carolina that provides night care hold an unannounced emergency drill during sleeping hours?
quote: An unannounced emergency drill shall be held during sleeping hours at least every 60 days.
notes: Applies to night care only. Regs 114-500 to 114-509 set no general fire drill frequency for centers: 114-505.H(1) requires compliance with State Fire Marshal regulations and 114-505.H(3) requires a written evacuation plan.

question: In what position must infants be placed to sleep at a licensed child care center in South Carolina?
quote: Sleeping (a) Infants shall be placed on their backs to sleep.
notes: No exception for other positions is stated.

question: When a child has an accident or injury at a licensed child care center in South Carolina that requires professional medical treatment (but not emergency treatment), within how many hours must the center give written notification to the Department?
quote: The center shall report the following incidents to the parents/guardians immediately and provide written notification to the Department within 48 hours after the occurrence: (a) Accidents or injuries involving any child occurring at the center requiring professional medical treatment
notes: Parents must be told immediately. Injuries requiring emergency professional medical treatment must be reported to the Department immediately (114-503.D(2)(c)).

question: What immunization document must be in the health record kept for each child enrolled at a licensed child care center in South Carolina?
answer: A current South Carolina certificate of immunization.
quote: A health record shall be maintained in the center for each child enrolled, and it shall include all of the following information: ... (b) A current South Carolina certificate of Immunization;
notes: The rule sets no deadline in days. A parent's statement of the child's health is required within 30 days before admission (114-505.A(1)), and parents are told at admission that they must obtain immunizations (114-503.F(3)(d)).

question: At minimum, how many people certified in pediatric first aid (including rescue breathing, CPR, and management of a blocked airway) must be present in a licensed child care center in South Carolina at all times when children are in care?
quote: At least one person who is certified in pediatric first aid, including rescue breathing, CPR, and management of a blocked airway shall be present in the center at all times when children are in care, and during group outings or field trips.
notes: Also required during group outings and field trips. Having a CPR-certified teacher in each infant and toddler classroom is only recommended.

question: How much space must there be on two sides of each crib at a licensed child care center in South Carolina?
quote: Cribs shall be spaced so that there is at least three feet of space on two sides of the crib.
notes: Cribs also may not be placed so one child can reach into another child's crib. No spacing rule for cots or mats was found.

question: How long is a regular license issued to a licensed child care center in South Carolina valid?
quote: A regular license/regular approval issued by the Department to the child care center shall be valid for two years from date of issuance
notes: A change in location, ownership or sponsorship voids the license. A provisional license runs for the period set to correct deficiencies (114-502.B(2)).

question: During nap time at a licensed child care center in South Carolina, provided at least one other staff person is readily available, what is the staff-to-child ratio for children four years and older? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: During nap times the following ratios apply as long as at least one other staff person is readily available: NAP TIME STAFF:CHILD RATIOS ... Four years and older ... 1:34
notes: The awake ratio for four-to-five-year-olds is 1:17. Night care uses the same ratios during sleeping hours (114-509.C(1)(b)).

question: While children four to five years old are swimming or wading at a licensed child care center in South Carolina, what staff-to-child ratio applies? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: The following staffing ratios apply at all times while children are swimming or wading. ... Four to five years ... Staff:Child Ratio ... 1:6
notes: Also applies near a water body that poses a risk for the child's age. Children five and older: 2:25. Swimming must be supervised by someone with current lifeguard certification, unless all staff can quickly reach any child without swimming (114-504.D(2)).

question: At a licensed child care center in South Carolina, which ratio applies to a mixed-age group in the same room that includes one or more infants or toddlers?
answer: The ratio for the youngest child in the group.
quote: For mixed age groups, with one or more infants or toddlers, the ratios applicable to the youngest child in the group apply.
notes: Without infants or toddlers, a mixed-age group uses the ratio for the age of the majority (114-504.B(2)).

question: When must the Department be notified of an accident or injury to a child at a licensed child care center in South Carolina that requires emergency professional medical treatment?
quote: The following incidents shall be reported to the Department immediately and may be investigated by the Department: ... (c) Accidents or injuries involving any child occurring at the center requiring emergency professional medical treatment;
notes: Non-emergency injuries needing professional medical treatment get written notice within 48 hours (114-503.D(1)(a)).

question: Under what conditions may a 17-year-old work as a teacher/caregiver at a licensed child care center in South Carolina?
answer: If they have a GED or high school diploma and are continuously supervised by a qualified teacher/caregiver who is in the room at all times.
quote: Exception: A teacher/caregiver may be 17 years of age if he/she has received his/her GED or high school diploma and is continuously supervised by a qualified teacher/caregiver who is in the room at all times.
notes: The general minimum age is 18 (114-503.K(4)(a)(i)).
